questions.question: A patient has a positive pregnancy test, severe unilateral pelvic pain, shoulder pain, dizziness, and near-syncope. What is the priority?
choices: Emergency evaluation for possible ruptured ectopic pregnancy or another hemorrhagic emergency
Routine follow-up after the next menstrual period
Reassurance because vaginal bleeding is only light
Delay evaluation until a repeat home pregnancy test is available
questions.explanation: Positive pregnancy with severe pain, shoulder pain, weakness, dizziness, or syncope may indicate ruptured ectopic pregnancy and life-threatening internal bleeding. Minimal vaginal bleeding does not rule out danger.

questions.question: Which statement about ectopic-pregnancy risk is most accurate?
choices: Ectopic pregnancy occurs only after assisted reproduction
It is ruled out when a patient has no prior pelvic infection or surgery
Prior ectopic pregnancy, tubal disease, pelvic infection, surgery, infertility, and smoking can increase risk, but many patients have no known risk factors
Shoulder pain is never related to ectopic pregnancy
questions.explanation: Risk factors can raise suspicion, but about half of people with ectopic pregnancy have no known risk factors. Absence of risk factors must not end the assessment.

questions.question: What is the best interpretation of first-trimester spotting and cramping?
choices: It proves early pregnancy loss
It may occur in a viable pregnancy, early loss, ectopic pregnancy, or another condition, so assessment and safety-netting are needed
It is always normal and needs no follow-up
It identifies the location of the pregnancy
questions.explanation: Bleeding and cramping have overlapping causes. They cannot independently determine pregnancy location or viability.

questions.question: Why is a single quantitative serum hCG value insufficient to diagnose pregnancy location or viability?
choices: hCG has no role in early-pregnancy assessment
One value cannot reliably establish location or trajectory; serial hCG and ultrasound may be needed in clinical context
A single hCG value confirms a normal intrauterine pregnancy
hCG testing is only useful after delivery
questions.explanation: Quantitative hCG is time-linked information. In stable patients with uncertainty, serial values and ultrasound can help clarify pregnancy location and trajectory.

questions.question: A patient has a positive pregnancy test, mild cramping, spotting, and an ultrasound that does not identify a pregnancy location. The patient is stable. Which term and plan are most appropriate?
choices: Confirmed normal intrauterine pregnancy; no follow-up is needed
Confirmed miscarriage; start treatment immediately
Pregnancy of unknown location; arrange a specific serial hCG and repeat-ultrasound pathway with explicit emergency precautions
Ectopic pregnancy is excluded because the patient is stable
questions.explanation: Pregnancy of unknown location is a safety status, not a final diagnosis. It can represent early intrauterine pregnancy, early loss, or ectopic pregnancy and requires closed-loop follow-up.

questions.question: Why should a clinician obtain diagnostic certainty before treating suspected early pregnancy loss when the patient is stable?
choices: Bleeding and cramping can overlap with viable intrauterine pregnancy and ectopic pregnancy, so premature treatment can cause harm
Early pregnancy loss can be confirmed by symptoms alone
Ultrasound and serial testing have no role in diagnostic uncertainty
Patient preference is irrelevant once bleeding occurs
questions.explanation: Before treatment, viable intrauterine pregnancy and ectopic pregnancy must be considered. History, examination, ultrasound, and serial hCG may be needed to reach sufficient certainty.

questions.question: A stable patient with early pregnancy bleeding has a history of anticoagulant use and increasing pad use. What additional FNP concern is most important?
choices: Bleeding severity and hemorrhage risk may be increased, so assess urgency and arrange appropriate evaluation rather than treating the visit as routine
Anticoagulant use has no relevance to pregnancy bleeding
The patient should stop anticoagulation independently at home
Only fetal sex determines the urgency
questions.explanation: Anticoagulant exposure, heavy bleeding, anemia symptoms, or hemodynamic change can increase concern for hemorrhage. Medication changes require coordinated, patient-specific management.

questions.question: Which action best demonstrates closed-loop care for a stable patient with pregnancy of unknown location?
choices: Tell the patient to return if worried, without arranging testing
Document who reviews each result, when repeat testing occurs, how the patient will be reached, and which symptoms require emergency care
Assume the patient will schedule follow-up independently
Avoid discussing emergency precautions to reduce anxiety
questions.explanation: Pregnancy of unknown location can become dangerous if follow-up is missed. Closed-loop plans assign responsibility, timing, communication, and explicit return precautions.

questions.question: Which statement about early-pregnancy physical examination is most appropriate?
choices: A pelvic examination should be forced before any care can be provided
Examination findings alone can rule out ectopic pregnancy
In a stable patient, examination should be purposeful, consent-based, and trauma-informed; in an unstable patient, it must not delay emergency transfer
No vital signs are needed when the pregnancy test is positive
questions.explanation: The examination should answer a clinical question and respect consent. Vital signs and stability come first, and unstable patients need emergency care without avoidable delay.

questions.question: Which patient statement requires the clearest immediate emergency safety instruction?
choices: I have a small amount of spotting and no pain
I have a positive test, my pain suddenly became severe, and I feel like I may faint
I would like to discuss prenatal vitamins next month
I need a copy of my prior laboratory results
questions.explanation: Sudden severe pain with presyncope after a positive pregnancy test is an emergency pattern. The patient should seek immediate emergency evaluation and not drive if feeling faint or unstable.
